fact_text: Shariah-compliant investing requires that an investment be free of interest, gambling-type uncertainty, and haram goods or businesses; an investment that passes these tests is called Islamic investing.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: The stock market itself is neither halal nor haram; whether it is permissible depends on the transactions carried out in it.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: Share settlement in Pakistan is T+1, so delivery of purchased shares arrives one day after the trade, and the speaker says the regulator sped this up from T+2.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: Same-day buying and selling (day trading) is ruled impermissible because Shariah requires taking ownership and possession of shares before any resale.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: Short selling is ruled non-compliant because the seller neither owns nor possesses the shares being sold, and Shariah requires both ownership and possession before a sale.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: Margin trading is an interest-based loan transaction in which a broker or bank finances the investor's share purchase and the investor pays interest, so the speaker advises against it.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: A Shariah alternative to margin trading is murabaha: the financier buys the shares, takes possession, and then sells them to the investor on deferred terms.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: The first Shariah screen asks whether a company's core business is permissible: textile, auto, furniture and oil makers pass, while conventional banks, insurers, wine makers and cinemas fail.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: A minority shareholder may hold a company whose interest-bearing debt is below 33% of its total assets; the scholars set this threshold.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: The interest-debt threshold was cut from 37% to 33% of total assets, and scholars plan further cuts to 30%, 25% and 20%, with the long-run aim of zero.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: The second screen caps non-permissible (haram) income at 5% of total revenue; a company above that level is excluded, while one below it may be held if its interest income is purified.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: Management and board members may not take any interest income at all, even one rupee; the 33% and 5% tolerances apply only to ordinary minority shareholders.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: The thresholds are meant to steer investors toward companies with less interest exposure and to push managements to reduce their interest dealings over time.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: Shareholders must give to charity the portion of a dividend equal to the interest income the company earned, even when the company itself is Shariah-compliant.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: The interest share used for purification is disclosed in a company's financial statements, and the PSX Shariah-compliant list also carries this information.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: A company that places no money in conventional interest-bearing instruments has no interest in its dividends, so its dividends need no purification.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: The Pakistan Stock Exchange publishes a Shariah-compliant company list every six months, prepared with Meezan Bank, so investors can use it instead of checking balance sheets.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: If a holding drops off the compliant list at a review, the speaker's rule is to sell it promptly when the position is at break-even or in profit.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: A holding at a loss after the company turns non-compliant may be kept until the price recovers to the purchase cost, but only while the company's core business remains permissible.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: Shares bought to earn capital gains are treated as trading assets, so zakat is due on their full current market value, not the purchase price.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: Illustration: OGDC shares bought at 500 rupees and worth 550 rupees on the zakat date would attract zakat on the 550 rupee market value for a capital-gain holder.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: A long-term holder who wants dividends pays zakat only on the zakatable share of the company's assets from its balance sheet, applied to the market value of the shares.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: Illustration: if half of a company's assets are zakatable and the share is worth 500 rupees, zakat is due on 250 rupees of that value.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: When the asset split is hard to compute, paying zakat on the full market value is the advised option, since it pays more and is the safer choice.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: The securities regulator SECP asked brokerage houses to open Shariah-compliant (Islamic) windows, and Standard Capital Securities has launched one under Shariah advisers.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: An Islamic brokerage window is run under Shariah advisers with segregated investor cash and shares, and inside it short selling, futures selling and day trading are blocked by the system.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: Inside the Islamic window investor cash cannot be placed in a conventional bank, unlike ordinary broker accounts where client money may sit in an interest-paying bank.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: Outside the Islamic window an investor may day-trade even Shariah-compliant shares, because the window's restrictions apply only to accounts held inside it.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: An oil company's core business can be permissible while it still borrows from conventional banks, pays interest, and holds interest-bearing deposits, so these flows are screened separately.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: A conventional bank fails the core-business screen because lending at interest is its main activity, whereas Islamic banking offers financing and deposit products that comply with Shariah.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: A conventional insurance company fails the core-business screen, and takaful is the Shariah-compliant insurance alternative that the speaker points to.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: The speaker holds that Islam rejects get-rich-quick ideas: returns require patience, steady commitment and sound decisions, and no formula for overnight wealth exists.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)

fact_text: The speaker advises investing small amounts across several avenues rather than keeping savings idle, since money should circulate in the economy and not sit in lockers.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Is Stock Trading Halal or Haram in Islam? | Shariah Investing Explained | SCS Trade Podcast' (YouTube, 2026-10-28)
